pages: Other things being equal, as the price of a good rises, the quantity demanded falls.
The demand curve slopes downward from left to right.
Income, the prices of related goods, tastes and expectations shift the demand curve.
Substitutes: a rise in the price of one raises demand for the other.
As price rises, the quantity supplied rises.
The supply curve slopes upward from left to right.
Cost of production and technology shift supply.
Equilibrium price is where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.
Above equilibrium there is a surplus; below it there is a shortage.
A price ceiling is a legal maximum price, often causing shortages.
A price floor is a legal minimum price, such as a minimum wage.
